records.definition: Whether two representations concern the same token entity across time/state remains recoverable across an inter-engine boundary; identity is treated as continuity/equivalence evidence, not a predeclared object ID.

sources: NSM: THE SAME / OTHER; Goddard 2015 DOI 10.1093/oxfordhb/9780199677078.013.0018
linguistic.note: Language strongly preserves sameness/otherness, but lexical recurrence alone is insufficient. Session B (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, chip-20260908-cognitive-contract-litpull, REE_assembly 4390fc6c8a) grades this cell S: same-entity info is grammaticalised by >=3 structurally unlike devices reinvented in unrelated stocks; CULT-leaning caveat: discourse-disambiguation explains switch-reference equally well and no single device is universal (SYNTHESIS.md sec.3 item 1).

developmental.note: Infant individuation relies early on spatiotemporal continuity and later integrates properties/kind. Session B grades this cell S: numerical identity computed at 10-12 months from spatiotemporal information before kind information, pre-sortal-language (Xu & Carey 1996 overlaps this record's existing Xu citation); a separable computation with its own timetable, embodied at the FORMAT level (earliest inputs are spatiotemporal/body-in-space).

neural.note: Set from unassessed by Session B (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2): human MTL neurons fire for the same individual across picture, spoken name and written name, with invariance rising along the MTL hierarchy; grade S. Classification reading: modality-invariant FORMAT is architectural, but acquired cell-tuning CONTENT is cultural.

comparative.note: Set from unassessed by Session B (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2): cross-modal individual recognition in horses; mirror self-recognition in magpies, contested in cleaner wrasse; grade S. Ecological/social-species alternative live: conspecific identity is a shared ecological problem across all positive species tested (mammal, bird, contested teleost).

sources: Bisimulation/state-abstraction family; Zhang et al. 2021 arXiv:2006.10742
artificial_agent.note: Functional equivalence can be learned while discarding surface differences; not identical to token identity. Session B grades this cell s (partial, not S): the ablation criterion is met (object-level VoE fails without an object-level carrier) but the emergence criterion is only partly met, since object structure is usually supplied by the architecture; ARCH-leaning with the task-structure alternative live (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2).

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve content while deleting token identity across a boundary -> broken persistence, duplicated selves/objects, incoherent credit assignment and unstable memory integration.
records.alternative_explanation: Continuity may be reconstructed from transition/topology plus provenance rather than requiring a dedicated primitive.

session_b_reconciliation.classification_b: architectural-leaning, provisional; CULT-leaning caveat for the typology cell (discourse-disambiguation, no universal device); EMB-leaning caveat for developmental FORMAT (spatiotemporal-first) and comparative (social-species ecology); artificial-agent evidence graded s (ablation met, emergence only partial, object structure usually supplied)
session_b_reconciliation.disagreement_with_session_a: No verdict-direction disagreement -- both sessions read identity as supports/architectural-leaning overall. Session B's finer S/s grading downgrades the artificial_agent cell to partial (s), consistent with this record's existing note ('not identical to token identity') rather than contradicting it.

records.definition: Before/after/current/anticipated and trajectory order remain recoverable across boundaries, without assuming human-style metric time or tense.

sources: Bybee, Perkins & Pagliuca 1994 ISBN 9780226086651 (TAM reinvention, 25 phyla)
linguistic.note: Strong recurrence, but human tense systems vary greatly. Session B grades this cell S -- the only candidate with a preservation-under-lesion result in the typology domain: a tenseless language still obligatorily recovers temporal reference from aspect/adverbials/discourse even though tense itself is areal and absent in ~40% of languages (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2); directly relevant as a translatable-around precedent for MECH-545's within-boundary control (SYNTHESIS.md sec.3 item 6).

sources: Spelke core-knowledge programme; future/possibility developmental literature
Mascalzoni et al. 2013 PMID 23587033 (newborn causal-order preference)
developmental.note: Temporal sequencing and anticipation precede mature linguistic tense. Session B grades this cell S: causal launching order is preferred hours after birth; arbitrary order becomes reliable only ~28 months with verbal help. Reading: architectural for causal order, cultural for arbitrary order-as-content (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2).

sources: MacDonald et al. 2011 PMID 21867888 (hippocampal time cells)
Tsao et al. 2018 PMID 30158699 (LEC elapsed-time code)
Motala et al. 2018 PMID 29343859 (dissent: modality-specific sensory timing)
neural.note: Hippocampal sequence/time and trajectory structure support relational temporal coding. Session B grades this cell S, architectural at the episodic level; dissent: sensory-level timing rate after-effects do not transfer across vision/audition/touch, i.e. embodied/modality-specific at the sensory-timing level (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 9).

sources: Schnell et al. 2021 PMID 34403629 (cuttlefish, no hippocampus)
comparative.note: Future-oriented behaviour appears outside humans, although explicit mental-time-travel interpretations remain debated. Session B grades this cell S: what-where-when preserved with age in cuttlefish (no hippocampus) as well as corvids; dissent: trace-strength could produce the same behaviour without a represented relation, a translatable-around argument MECH-545's control must rule out (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 6).

sources: Bi & Zhou 2020 PMID 32341153 (elapsed time emerges unspecified in RNNs)
Lipinski et al. 2023 arXiv:2310.06555 (temporal reference needs architecture, not task pressure)
artificial_agent.note: Predictive state representations preserve transition/future structure. Session B grades this cell S -- one of only two artificial-agent cells across all five candidates that meets genuine emergence (not just ablation): elapsed time emerges unspecified as trajectory position and stays decodable when multiplexed with non-temporal content; temporal reference in emergent communication needed an architectural change, not task pressure (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 items 7-8).

ree.note: Content-level owners; boundary form remains to be lesioned.

records.lesion_prediction: Content without temporal relation -> cause/effect inversion, present/anticipated confusion, planning failure and memory/prediction contamination.
records.alternative_explanation: Some temporal information may be implicit in transition geometry rather than carried as a distinct coordinate.

session_b_reconciliation.quorum_S_of_5: 5 (5) -- full quorum, and the only candidate with a preservation-under-lesion typology result
session_b_reconciliation.classification_b: architectural (provisional) for causal/episodic order; cultural for tense and arbitrary order-as-content; embodied at the sensory-timing level -- matches this record's existing classification/alternative_explanation closely
session_b_reconciliation.disagreement_with_session_a: No material disagreement; Session B corroborates Session A's architectural/embodied split and adds the tenseless-language and cuttlefish results as the domain's strongest translatable-around and least-embodiment-confounded evidence respectively.

records.definition: The receiving system can recover whether content is externally constrained, remembered, simulated, counterfactual, candidate or currently treated as obtaining/committed.

sources: NSM: TRUE / MAYBE / CAN / IF; evidentiality and modality literature
de Haan 2013 WALS ch. 77-78 (evidentiality areal, not genetic)
Bybee 1998 Anthropological Linguistics 40:257-271 (irrealis not one category)
von Prince, Krajinovic & Krifka 2022 DOI 10.1353/lan.2022.0009 (splits possible vs counterfactual)
linguistic.note: Languages repeatedly encode epistemic/modal distinctions, but packaging varies. Session B grades this cell s, not S (weaker than this record's existing verdict): evidentiality is grammaticalised in 237/418 languages but almost absent from Africa and reads as areal rather than genetic; 'irrealis' is rejected as a coherent single category and splits into possible vs counterfactual -- CULT-leaning, and the named dissent is that reality-status marking looks diffused-cultural on the typological evidence alone (SYNTHESIS.md sec.3 items 1-2).

developmental.note: Source monitoring and explicit modal concepts develop; minimal alternative-state handling may precede them. Session B grades this cell S: 15-month-olds track pretend-episode consistency without confusing it with the real objects, supporting a coarse actual/not-actual marker; the fuller four-way distinction is protracted, knowledge-dependent and degrades under emotion -- consistent with this record's own reservation about the four-way relation as stated (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.4).

sources: Garrison et al. 2015 PMID 26573408 (paracingulate sulcus predicts hallucination modality-independently)
Dijkstra & Fleming 2023 PMID 36959279 (overlaps this record's Dijkstra, Kok & Fleming 2022 citation)
neural.note: Perception/imagination overlap makes higher-order source/status inference necessary. Session B grades this cell S: a subsystem-independent DECISION (paracingulate morphology predicts hallucination regardless of sensory modality); named dissent qualifies the mechanism as reconstruction from a shared graded signal rather than a protected tag -- vivid imagery is judged real (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 3).

sources: Crystal et al. 2013 PMID 23394830 (source-of-encounter memory, rats)
comparative.note: Set from unassessed by Session B (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2), grade s not S: source-of-encounter memory is separably lesionable in rats (CA3 inactivation abolishes it), but searches for imagined-vs-perceived discrimination or a DRM-analogue false-memory task in any non-human species returned zero records -- the observed-vs-imagined contrast this candidate names is effectively absent, not merely weak, in this domain.

artificial_agent.note: Set from unassessed by Session B (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2), grade s not S: untagged model-generated transitions collapse model-based RL, and separating real/imagined buffers with bounded imagination depth is the standard fix (ablation criterion met); no case found of an agent inventing an observed/imagined marker unprompted (emergence criterion not met).

records.lesion_prediction: Delete source/status while preserving content -> false commitment to imagined states, confabulation-like behaviour and counterfactual/experience contamination.
records.alternative_explanation: Likely not one primitive: provenance/source and branch/actuality/commitment status may be separable coordinates.

session_b_reconciliation.quorum_S_of_5: 2 (5 counting s) -- at the strict quorum threshold
session_b_reconciliation.classification_b: uncertain; architectural-leaning ONLY for a coarse actual/not-actual marker; the four-way relation (observed/remembered/imagined/counterfactual) as MECH-545 currently states it is unsupported as a SINGLE invariant and should be split into >=2-3 sub-relations (actual/possible/counterfactual per typology; source-of-encounter provenance per comparative/neural)
session_b_reconciliation.disagreement_with_session_a: Verdict-level disagreement on the linguistic cell: this record already carries 'supports' where Session B grades the same evidence s (areal/cultural-leaning, irrealis not coherent) -- kept as this record's verdict per merge policy, Session B's downgrade recorded in the linguistic note above. Structural convergence, not conflict, at the whole-candidate level: this record's own alternative_explanation already floats 'provenance/source and branch/actuality/commitment status may be separable coordinates,' and Session B independently arrives at the same split (>=2-3 relations, not one), naming it as the pull's most useful output for MECH-545's lesion design (SYNTHESIS.md sec.1, sec.3 item 3, sec.5).

records.definition: Actor/source, action, predicted consequence and controllability relations can be reconstructed across boundaries.

sources: NSM: I / YOU / DO / HAPPEN; recurrent argument/agent structure
Comrie 2013 WALS ch. 98 (case distinction absent in >50% of 190 languages)
linguistic.note: Language externalises agency strongly but does not show agency is atomic. Session B grades this cell S: the relation is always recoverable though its grammatical vehicle is highly variable; ARCH-leaning, with an EMB-live caveat that near-universality is also what a shared action problem across languages would predict (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2).

sources: Goal representation in the infant brain PMC3898941
Gergely et al. 1995 PMID 7554793 (goal attribution to a bodiless 2-D agent, 12mo)
developmental.note: Goal-directed agent representations occur early. Session B grades this cell S, and flags the bodiless-2-D-agent result (12-month-olds attribute goal-directed agency to a shape with no body from efficient action-to-goal structure alone) as the decisive datum for a body-independent, architectural reading (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2).

sources: Reznik et al. 2014 PMID 24898564 (dissent: effector-specific, can enhance not suppress)
neural.note: Sense of agency is built from prospective and retrospective components. Session B grades this cell S: corollary discharge is a distinction-retaining translation mechanism recurring across phyla; dissent: the agency signal is effector-specific and can enhance rather than suppress -- architectural for the relation, embodied for the implementation (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 9).

sources: Poulet & Hedwig 2006 PMID 16439660 (single corollary-discharge interneuron, cricket)
Bell et al. 1997 PMID 9153391 / 1993 PMID 8506312 (mormyrid fish)
comparative.note: Causal/goal-directed behaviour is cross-species, with inferential interpretation debated. Session B grades this cell S and names it the least embodiment-confounded cell in the whole pull: insect, electric fish and primate -- three unrelated modalities/phyla (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2).

sources: Choi et al. 2019 arXiv:1811.01483 (controllable factor from own-action prediction; collapse without it)
Thomas et al. 2017 arXiv:1708.01289 (controllability as organising variable)
artificial_agent.note: Action structure can separate controllable/task-relevant from uncontrolled observation components. Session B grades this cell S and names it the only cell in the artificial-agents domain, across all five candidates, where BOTH the ablation AND emergence admissibility tests are met (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 7).

records.lesion_prediction: Events remain representable but actor/control relation is lost -> poor action learning, attribution errors and failed responsibility/intentional planning.
records.alternative_explanation: Evidence increasingly favors a composite of source/ownership + action + consequence + causal/control relation rather than an irreducible AGENCY primitive.

session_b_reconciliation.quorum_S_of_5: 5 (5) -- full quorum, least embodiment-confounded evidence in the pull
session_b_reconciliation.classification_b: architectural (provisional; the strongest case of the five candidates) for the coarse self-caused/not-self-caused primitive; derived structure (intention, responsibility, social attribution) explicitly not assessed
session_b_reconciliation.disagreement_with_session_a: Classification-level disagreement: this record's existing classification is 'uncertain' with confidence 'high-recurrence-composite,' and its alternative_explanation states the evidence 'increasingly favors a composite ... rather than an irreducible AGENCY primitive.' Session B reads the SAME evidence as the strongest architectural case of the five (full quorum, least embodied confound) for the coarse self-caused/not-self-caused primitive specifically, while agreeing the DERIVED structure (intention, responsibility, social attribution) is a separate, unassessed question. This record's classification/confidence fields are left unchanged per merge policy; flagged here for governance to reconcile explicitly rather than silently favouring either session.

records.definition: Reliability/uncertainty attached to content or status remains usable by the receiver; translation confidence may need to be represented separately from content confidence.

sources: Boye 2012 DOI 10.1515/9783110219036 (epistemic domain fused with evidentiality)
linguistic.note: Human language repeatedly marks uncertainty but this is not enough to establish architecture. Session B grades this cell s, not S: the epistemic meaning domain is cross-linguistically coherent but comprises two subdomains (certainty, information source) that cluster into FUSED systems, and mirativity as a grammaticalised prediction-error marker is itself contested as a category -- named dissent: CONFIDENCE and REALITY STATUS are frequently fused in the morphology, arguing against treating them as two separately preserved invariants without an explicit dissociation control (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 4).

sources: Gori et al. 2008 PMID 18450446 (dissent: reliability-weighted integration absent until ~8y)
developmental.note: Possibility judgments interact with confidence/uncertainty monitoring across development. Session B grades this cell S for confidence-as-FLAG only: non-verbal metacognitive sensitivity with an adult-homologous ERN is present at 12-18 months; dissent: reliability-weighted visual-haptic integration (confidence-as-WEIGHT) is absent until ~8 years -- only the flag has developmental precedence (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 5).

sources: Fleming 2024 Annual Review of Psychology DOI 10.1146/annurev-psych-022423-032425
de Gardelle, Le Corre & Mamassian 2016 PMID 26808061 (common currency, vision/audition)
Morales, Lau & Fleming 2018 PMID 29519851 (domain-general + domain-specific PFC)
neural.note: Confidence/metacognition is separable from first-order content. Session B grades this cell S: confidence is compared across vision and audition as precisely as within a task, a common currency partly reconstructed at the neural level; qualification: domain-general AND domain-specific confidence representations coexist in PFC (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2).

comparative.note: Metacognition-like behaviour exists but associative explanations remain live. Session B grades this cell S and flags it as translatable-around-contested: a chosen-vs-forced opt-out signature spans rhesus, rats and honeybees, but a first-order associative account remains live and pigeons repeatedly fail the task -- species dissociation is itself named as dissenting evidence against a required invariant (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 10).

sources: uncertainty-aware world-model and Information Bottleneck literature
Chua et al. 2018 arXiv:1805.12114 (factorial ablation, aleatoric+epistemic uncertainty separately necessary)
Buckman et al. 2018 arXiv:1807.01675 (per-example uncertainty weighting)
artificial_agent.note: Engineering precedent is strong, but direct emergent contract evidence is not yet available. Session B grades this cell s, consistent with this record's existing note: the ablation criterion is met but emergent-communication agents modulate effort by difficulty without any verified explicit confidence value in the channel -- no emergence (SYNTHESIS.md sec.2, sec.3 item 7).

ree.note: Content precision exists; translation confidence is a recorded substrate gap.

records.lesion_prediction: Content translates but reliability does not -> overcommitment, underreaction to reliable predictions and failed precision-sensitive integration.
records.alternative_explanation: May be control metadata rather than a semantic contract primitive; translation confidence may require a distinct meta-interface quantity.

session_b_reconciliation.quorum_S_of_5: 3 (5 counting s), all three S cells qualified
session_b_reconciliation.classification_b: split -- confidence-as-FLAG architectural (provisional); confidence-as-WEIGHT/precision-integration uncertain, embodied/calibration-dependent (not developmentally present until ~8 years)
session_b_reconciliation.disagreement_with_session_a: Session B splits this record's single candidate into two sub-relations (flag vs weight) where this record currently carries one undifferentiated verdict set per domain and a single classification ('uncertain') / confidence ('moderate'). This record's own 'ree' note already anticipates the split ('translation confidence is a recorded substrate gap' distinct from content precision), so the two sessions converge on the SHAPE of the split even though this record has not yet been restructured to carry it; flagged for governance/MECH-545 to decide whether the ledger record itself should be split into confidence_flag and confidence_weight sub-candidates (SYNTHESIS.md sec.1, sec.3 item 5, sec.4).

records.definition: Same/different/like relations among representations can be recovered independently of the specific entities filling the relation.

sources: Holden 2019 DOI 10.1086/700319 as corrective for broader prime claims
linguistic.note: Same/other/similarity is stronger than KIND/PART as a cross-linguistic relational family.

neural.note: Relational knowledge supports reasoning, categorisation, planning, quantification and language.

comparative.note: A dedicated comparative same/different pull remains useful.

ree.note: No dedicated REE contract owner yet; likely overlaps identity and mutual-legibility work.

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve entity content but delete equivalence relations -> inability to transfer learned structure across exemplars, degraded analogy/generalisation and unnecessary duplication of schemas.
records.alternative_explanation: Could be an operation over relational topology rather than a separate primitive; token identity and type-level similarity may share a deeper equivalence calculus.

records.definition: Adjacency, transition and structural relations among states/entities remain recoverable even when sensory or engine-specific coordinates remap.

sources: Grambank hierarchical-universal result: Nature Human Behaviour s41562-025-02325-z
linguistic.note: Hierarchical relations survive stronger phylogenetic/geographic controls better than many surface universals; indirect evidence only.

developmental.note: Infants can abstract relations beyond specific arguments.

neural.note: Hippocampal/entorhinal map-like codes generalise beyond physical space; reusable structure can bind to remapped content.

comparative.note: Physical-map evidence is strong; abstraction to nonspatial relation is less established comparatively.

artificial_agent.note: Bisimulation and successor representations explicitly preserve behaviorally/predictively relevant transition structure while discarding surface detail.

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve local feature content but scramble relational/transition topology -> poor transfer, planning failures and loss of cross-context structural generalisation despite intact recognition.
records.alternative_explanation: Risk of becoming vacuous if formulated too broadly; must be operationalised by specific recoverable transition/adjacency relations.

records.definition: Ordered comparison such as more/less, larger/smaller or stronger/weaker can survive translation; exact numerosity is treated as a possible specialisation rather than the primitive.

sources: NSM: ONE / TWO / MUCH-MANY / LITTLE-FEW / MORE / BIG / SMALL

developmental.note: Infants show abstract approximate number representations before language.

neural.note: Abstract number coding generalises across modalities in primate parieto-frontal systems.

comparative.note: Numerosity/magnitude sensitivity is widespread across distant taxa.

sources: NeurIPS 2020 On Numerosity of Deep Neural Networks corrective result
artificial_agent.note: Numerosity can emerge under some regimes but spontaneous DNN number-sense claims require strong controls.

ree.note: Quantities are present in the substrate but no evidence yet that a generic magnitude relation is a boundary invariant.

records.lesion_prediction: Delete ordered magnitude while preserving categorical identity -> failures in comparing resource amounts, confidence strengths and graded harms/benefits while nominal recognition remains intact.
records.alternative_explanation: May be an ecological/agentic convenience of organisms operating over quantities rather than a requirement of unified cognition itself.

records.definition: Signed evaluative relation to an organism's viability/preferences (beneficial-harmful, appetitive-aversive) can be compared across represented outcomes.

sources: Holden 2019 DOI 10.1086/700319 notes BAD as problematic in Dene
linguistic.note: Independent hypothesis family plus an important lexical-universality caution.

developmental.note: Early evaluative preferences exist, but rich moral interpretation is contested.

neural.note: Common-currency value evidence is strong, while value, salience, learning and incentive motivation must be dissociated.

sources: goal-directed outcome-devaluation literature; Dolan & Dayan 2013 PMID 24139036
comparative.note: Animals alter action when represented outcome value changes.

artificial_agent.note: Common in agent design but usually supplied by task objective rather than spontaneously discovered.

ree.note: Strong REE necessity for ethical/viability agency.

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve outcome identity and transition structure but delete signed value -> coherent prediction without principled preference, impaired tradeoff and devaluation sensitivity.
records.alternative_explanation: Likely mandatory for viability-regulating agents but not yet shown to be substrate-universal for every possible unified cognitive system.

records.definition: A represented future/outcome state is marked as action-organising relative to value/need and controllability.

linguistic.note: Strong linguistic recurrence but not evidence of atomicity.

sources: Goal representation in the infant brain PMC3898941
developmental.note: Goal-directed action representations are present in infancy.

sources: O'Doherty et al. 2017 Annual Review of Psychology
neural.note: Goal-directed control depends on represented action-outcome structure and current outcome value.

comparative.note: Goal-directed action is robustly studied in rodents and other animals.

artificial_agent.note: Goal-conditioned agents can learn transferable state abstractions.

ree.note: Goals are explicit in REE trajectory evaluation.

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve future-state and value content but delete target/action-organising relation -> intact prediction and valuation with aimless or unstable policy selection.
records.alternative_explanation: Likely decomposes into prospective state + value/need + controllability + priority/commitment rather than being primitive.

records.definition: A represented relation/state can be marked as not obtaining or an expected event can be represented as absent, distinct from mere lack of information.

linguistic.note: Negation is universal in human thought/language; acquisition study supports a linguistic rather than conceptual bottleneck for English negation words.

developmental.note: Whether infancy begins with full logical negation or narrower rejection/non-existence remains open.

comparative.note: Critical next question: non-linguistic representation of non-occurrence/absence across species.

artificial_agent.note: Could be tested directly in predictive agents via omitted expected events.

sources: language thought: prediction-error/correction 'no'; predictive error machinery

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve positive content but delete non-obtaining/absence -> inability to reject hypotheses, represent missing expected events or distinguish not-X from unknown-X.
records.alternative_explanation: May emerge from prediction-error plus alternative-state representation rather than requiring a standalone operator.

records.definition: The system can distinguish an obtaining state from one or more generated alternatives and retain whether an alternative is merely candidate, counterfactual, hypothetical or impossible/ruled out.

linguistic.note: Explicit modal packaging may be later than minimal alternative handling.

developmental.note: Developmental dissociation between minimal alternatives and explicit modal concepts is highly informative.

neural.note: Counterfactual networks represent alternative options/values and link them to control/planning.

comparative.note: Future-oriented behaviour exists outside humans; explicit modal concepts remain unproven.

sources: model-based world models and rollout agents; successor/bisimulation families
artificial_agent.note: Alternative trajectories are standard computational objects, but status tagging varies.

records.lesion_prediction: Generated alternatives remain content-rich but lose branch/status -> imagined/counterfactual trajectories contaminate actual belief or are committed to prematurely.
records.alternative_explanation: Likely a family of statuses rather than one modal primitive; explicit possibility/necessity concepts may be derived later.

records.definition: A trajectory/action representation carries whether it is exploratory, intended, socially relied upon or irreversibly committed, so receivers do not confuse rehearsal with enacted policy.

sources: speech-act/promising literature; language thought externalises commitments
linguistic.note: Commitment need not be linguistically explicit.

sources: Just how joint is joint action in infancy? PMID 25164940
developmental.note: Minimal/implicit commitment can be studied before mature explicit promises.

neural.note: Dedicated neural commitment/irreversibility pull still useful.

sources: Every product needs a process: unpacking joint commitment across species PMID 35876205
comparative.note: Cross-species approach argues commitment is gradual and process-based; strength of non-human evidence varies.

artificial_agent.note: Could be operationalised directly at policy/rehearsal boundaries.

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve trajectory content but delete commitment status -> rehearsal treated as action, unstable promises/policies, or inability to maintain action through transient preference changes.
records.alternative_explanation: Probably a derived status over trajectory + agent + expectation + persistence, not a primitive; may only be mandatory at selected boundaries.

records.definition: Representations can carry an attentional/resource-allocation priority distinct from signed value and from epistemic confidence.

linguistic.note: Deixis and emphasis may externalise priority, but no dedicated typological case yet.

sources: Neurodevelopment of Attention, Learning, and Memory Systems in Infancy DOI 10.1146/annurev-devpsych-120321-011300
developmental.note: Attention and learning interact from infancy; priority systems develop on separable timescales.

sources: Kahnt & Tobler 2017 Reward, Value, and Salience
neural.note: Priority integrates bottom-up salience with goal relevance; value and salience dissociate experimentally.

comparative.note: Likely broad but not yet ledger-grade.

sources: attention/priority mechanisms in learned agents; multi-task sufficient-representation literature
artificial_agent.note: Engineering analogy strong but emergent universality untested.

ree.note: REE already routes attention/gain, but cross-engine priority preservation is untested.

records.lesion_prediction: Preserve value and confidence but delete relevance/priority -> correct beliefs and preferences remain available yet computational resources are persistently allocated to the wrong representations.
records.alternative_explanation: Likely control metadata rather than semantic content; may be recomputed locally if enough value, surprise and goal information survives translation.
